blocking.title: AI nuclear use is still unseen in half the games and inert where a player sets it up: 8 of 17 unaided 30-year worlds see a burst (55 in 510 world-years), but only 3 of 17 before year 20 and 9 never, while 3 to 6 nations hold 118 to 163 warheads; France and Poland, given 10 warheads each in the editor and overrun (capitals taken), never strike in 120 to 150 days; some strikes hit near-empty or third-party places (Nepal, 1,000 dead; China on one Xinjiang point four times in 4 days, 641,568 then 18,088, 1,554 and 566 dead)
blocking.fix: nukesAllowed passes for them (src/sim/systems/nuclear.ts:150, settings only), so the utility never turns positive for an overrun holder in 1938: make a nuclear power losing a war for its life reach for the bomb in a visible share of games and earlier in the nuclear age; let warheads placed by the editor or God Mode be used by a desperate holder, or say in the editor why they will not be; do not strike a point already struck days before, nor small third parties for a thousand dead.

blocking.title: A sea battle's ticker row does not land on the fight (contradicts PLAN 7.10b): on seed 5591, with the battle live (view.seaBattles() non-empty, clicked at hour 41 of Germany's war on Britain), the row centres the view on dry land at Groningen at 364 m/px; the battle's own pair spans 23.3 cells (fleets on either side of the Dutch coast), the British and German fleets sit at opposite edges about 1,000 px apart, and in 6 s live at Speed x1 no gunfire is drawn; at 150, 40 and 15 m/px the centre has no ship
blocking.fix: A 'battle' between fleets 23 cells apart across land is not one a player can see: frame the point where ships actually exchange fire, with both near the centre, and never centre a sea battle on land (or make fleets close before they fight).

blocking.title: The Nuke tool's size is cosmetic (contradicts PLAN 7.16a): a hydrogen bomb kills 3 to 11 % more than an atomic one on the same point (Paris 554,827 against 588,117; London 751,186 / 790,283; Berlin 1,025,202 / 1,063,051; Moscow 161,530 / 179,694) and leaves a ruin that cannot be told apart at 300 m/px
blocking.fix: Give a thermonuclear bomb a yield on the order of tens to hundreds of times a fission one (detonate gets yieldN 2 against 1, radius x1.26), so its blast, toll, fallout and ruin are visibly larger.
